title: Deep Learning for BioImaging: What Are We Really Learning?
abstract: arXiv:2603.13377v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Representation learning has driven major advances in natural image analysis by enabling models to acquire high-level semantic features. In microscopy imaging, however, it remains unclear what current representation learning methods really learn. In this work, we conduct a systematic study of representation learning for the two most widely used and broadly available microscopy data types, representing critical scales in biology: cell culture and tissue imaging. We investigate whether, in contrast to natural images, existing models fail to consistently acquire high-level, biologically meaningful features. To this end, we introduce a set of simple yet revealing baselines on curated benchmarks, including untrained models and structural representations of cellular tissue. translated_title: 深度学习在生物成像中的应用：我们真正学到了什么？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.13377v2 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：表征学习通过使模型获取高级语义特征，推动了自然图像分析的重大进展。然而，在显微镜成像中，目前仍不清楚现有的表征学习方法真正学到了什么。在这项工作中，我们对两种最广泛使用且广泛可用的显微镜数据类型（代表生物学中的关键尺度：细胞培养和组织成像）进行了表征学习的系统研究。我们调查了与自然图像相比，现有模型是否未能一致地获取高级的、具有生物学意义的特征。为此，我们在精选基准上引入了一组简单但具有启示性的基线，包括未训练模型和细胞组织的结构表示。我们的结果表明，令人惊讶的是，在相当一部分评估设置中，这些基线与最先进的方法相当，这证明了...
tldr: 本文系统研究发现，在生物显微镜成像的表征学习中，未训练模型和简单结构基线在多项评估中与最先进方法表现相当，质疑了当前方法是否真正学到了生物学上有意义的特征。
en_tdlr: This systematic study reveals that in microscopy imaging, untrained and simple structural baselines perform comparably to state-of-the-art methods across many evaluations, questioning whether current representation learning truly captures biologically meaningful features.
